children.text: sarvadā sarvathā sarve yasya doṣā na santi ha |
children.translated_text: He in whom at all times, in every way, no faults whatsoever exist,
and in whom all virtues without exception are established — (1)

children.text: tam eva śaraṇaṃ gantuṃ taṃ stotuṃ tam upāsitum |
children.translated_text: to go to him alone for refuge, to praise him, to attend upon him,

children.text: tasyaiva śāsane sthātuṃ nyāyyaṃ yady asti cetanā || 2
children.translated_text: to abide in his teaching alone — this is fitting, if one has consciousness. (2)

children.text: savāsanāś ca te doṣā na santy ekasya tāyinaḥ |
children.translated_text: Those faults, together with their latent tendencies, do not exist in the one Protector;

children.text: sarve sarvavidaḥ santi guṇās te cānapāyinaḥ || 3
children.translated_text: all those virtues belong to the All-Knowing One, and they are imperishable. (3)
For even one who is thoroughly engaged in the actions of mind, speech, and body

children.text: saha dharmeṇa labhate kaś cid bhagavato 'ntaram || 4
children.translated_text: cannot find, in conformity with truth, any deficiency in the <s>Bhagavān</s>. (4)
I, having obtained human birth — that great festival accompanied by the true <s>Dharma</s> —
comparable to a turtle inserting its neck into a yoke's hole floating in the great ocean, (5)
shall I not make the most of this stream of eloquence, which is pursued by impermanence, uncertain due to gaps in <s>karma</s>,
and whose essence is to be seized? How could I not render this <s>Sarasvatī</s> (eloquence) fruitful? (6)
Thus, although knowing the qualities of the Sage, which range over innumerable objects,
this devotion to a fraction of them is undertaken, out of reverence for one's own purpose. (7)
Homage to you, the Self-Arisen One, whose deeds are abundant and wondrous,

children.text: yasya saṃkhyāprabhāvābhyāṃ na guṇeṣv asti niścayaḥ || 8
children.translated_text: in whose virtues there is no certainty as to their number or their power! (8)

children.text: iyanta iti nāsty anta īdṛśā iti kā kathā |
children.translated_text: 'They are this many' — there is no limit; 'they are of this kind' — what can be said?

children.text: puṇyā ity eva tu guṇān prati te mukharā vayam || 9
children.translated_text: That 'they are meritorious' — regarding your virtues, this alone is our eloquent utterance. (9)
Casting aside the deliberation 'is it bearable or unbearable?',

children.text: svayam abhyupapannaṃ te nirākrandam idaṃ jagat || 10
children.translated_text: this weeping world was approached by you of your own accord. (10)
You are virtuous without being asked; you are compassionate without cause;
you are a friend without introduction, and a kinsman without obligation. (11)

children.text: svamāṃsāny api dattāni vastuṣv anyeṣu kā kathā |
children.translated_text: You have given even your own flesh — what need to speak of other things?

children.text: prāṇair api tvayā sādho mānitaḥ praṇayī janaḥ || 12
children.translated_text: Even with your life, O virtuous one, you have honored those who sought your love. (12)

children.text: svaiḥ śarīraiḥ śarīrāṇi prāṇaiḥ prāṇāḥ śarīriṇām |
children.translated_text: With your own bodies you have ransomed the bodies, with your life-breaths the life-breaths of embodied beings
who had been seized by those who wished to kill — hundreds of times, by you. (13)
Not from fear of lower births, nor desiring a pleasant destination,
but solely through purity of intention was moral conduct made your own nature by you. (14)
Through always rejecting crooked actions and always cultivating upright ones,
you have become the sole resort of completely purified actions. (15)
Though afflicted many times, you, with a benevolent mind,
revealed your splendor amid afflictions; the afflicted were shown compassion. (16)

children.text: parārthe tyajataḥ prāṇān yā prītir abhavat tava |
children.translated_text: The joy that arose in you when giving up your life for others' sake —

children.text: na sā naṣṭopalabdheṣu prāṇeṣu prāṇināṃ bhavet || 17
children.translated_text: beings would not have such joy even upon recovering lives that had been lost. (17)
That you, heedless of pain, even while being cut apart again and again,

children.text: vadhakeṣv api sattveṣv kāruṇyam abhavat prabho || 18
children.translated_text: felt compassion even for the beings who were killing you, O Lord — (18)
of that jewel-mind of yours, which is the seed of perfect awakening,

children.text: tvam eva vīra sārajño dūre tasyetaro janaḥ || 19
children.translated_text: you alone, O hero, know the essence; other people are far from it. (19)

children.text: nākṛtvā duṣkaraṃ karma durlabham labhyate padam |
children.translated_text: 'Without performing difficult deeds, the hard-to-attain state cannot be obtained' —
thus, with disregard for yourself, energy was cultivated by you. (20)

children.text: viśeṣotkarṣaniyamo na kadā cid abhūt tava |
children.translated_text: There was never a limit to the excellence of your distinctions;
therefore, in you the gradation of degrees of distinction is cut off. (21)
Even in the most blissful and fruitful meditative absorptions, there was no attachment
in you, whose heart was constantly bound by great compassion. (22)

children.text: tvādṛśān pīḍayaty eva nānugṛhṇāti tat sukham |
children.translated_text: That happiness only pains those like you; it does not gratify them —

children.text: praṇītam api sadvṛtta yad asādhāraṇaṃ paraiḥ || 23
children.translated_text: even though exalted, O virtuous one — that which is not shared with others. (23)

children.text: vimiśrāt sāram ādattaṃ sarvaṃ pītam akalmaṣam |
children.translated_text: The essence was taken from what was mixed; all that was stainless was drunk in;

children.text: tvayā sūktaṃ duruktaṃ tu viṣavat parivarjitam || 24
children.translated_text: by you, well-spoken words were embraced, while ill-spoken words were shunned like poison. (24)
Buying well-spoken words even at the cost of life, O knower of the essence of jewels,
you strove toward awakening in each and every birth. (25)

children.text: iti tribhir asaṃkhyeyair evam udyacchatā tvayā |
children.translated_text: Thus, by you exerting yourself in this way through three incalculable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons),
with resolution as your companion, the unsurpassed state was attained. (26)
Without feeling envy toward the superior, nor despising the inferior,

children.text: agatvā sadṛśaiḥ spardhāṃ tvaṃ loke śreṣṭhatāṃ gataḥ || 27
children.translated_text: nor entering into rivalry with equals, you attained supremacy in the world. (27)

children.text: hetuṣv abhiniveśo 'bhūd guṇānāṃ na phaleṣu te |
children.translated_text: Your engagement was in the causes of virtues, not in their fruits;

children.text: tena samyakpratipadā tvayi niṣṭhāṃ guṇā gatāḥ || 28
children.translated_text: thereby, through right practice, virtues reached their culmination in you. (28)

children.text: tathātmā pracayaṃ nītas tvayā sucaritair yathā |
children.translated_text: In such a way was the self brought to fullness by you through good conduct, that
even the dust of your feet has become a field of merit. (29)
Having attenuated and uprooted faults, having increased and purified

children.text: guṇās tena sunītena parāṃ siddhiṃ tvam adhyagāḥ || 30
children.translated_text: virtues — through that excellent conduct, you attained the supreme accomplishment. (30)
So completely did you strike at faults
that not even a latent tendency of them remained in your mental continuum. (31)

children.text: tathā saṃbhṛtya saṃbhṛtya tvayātmany āhitā guṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: So thoroughly were virtues gathered and gathered again and placed in yourself by you,

children.text: pratirūpakam apy eṣāṃ yathā nānyatra dṛśyate || 32
children.translated_text: that not even a semblance of them is seen elsewhere. (32)
Subject to destruction and obstruction, limited in time and partial,
easily surpassed — all worldly objects of comparison are thus. (33)
For your virtues that are beyond duality, unfathomable, permanent, irreversible,

children.text: anuttarāṇāṃ kā tarhi guṇānām upamāstu te || 34
children.translated_text: and unsurpassed — what comparison could there be? (34)
The depth of the salt ocean becomes as shallow as a cow's hoofprint
when one beholds the unfathomable, boundless depth of your wisdom. (35)
The firmness of the earth becomes as light as the tip of a <s>śirīṣa</s> petal
when confronted with your immovable steadfastness in all <s>dharmas</s>. (36)
Of your light of knowledge, O Sage, which destroys the darkness of ignorance,

children.text: na ravir viṣaye bhūmiṃ khādyotīm api vindati || 37
children.translated_text: not even the sun finds a place in its domain — not even a firefly's light. (37)
The purities of the autumn moon, sky, and waters seem to take on impurity
in comparison with the purity of your speech, wisdom, and conduct. (38)

children.text: anena sarvaṃ vyākhyātaṃ yat kiṃ cit sādhu laukikam |
children.translated_text: By this, everything that is virtuous in the world has been explained;
for the qualities of the world, poor things, are far from the qualities of the <s>Buddha</s>. (39)

children.text: yasyaiva dharmaratnasya prāptyā prāptas tvam agratām |
children.translated_text: That very <s>Dharma</s>-jewel, by attaining which you attained preeminence —

children.text: tenaiva kevalaṃ sādho sāmyaṃ te tasya ca tvayā || 40
children.translated_text: with that alone, O virtuous one, is there equality between it and you. (40)
But if, under the mere pretext of one's own desire, some commonality were privately
alleged and spoken of [between you and others], that would be the speaker's extreme frivolity. (41)

children.text: pratanv iva hi paśyāmi dharmatām anucintayan |
children.translated_text: For reflecting on the nature of things, I see as if stretched thin —

children.text: sarvaṃ cāvarjitaṃ māravijayaṃ prati te jagat || 42
children.translated_text: yet all the world was won over by you in your victory over <s>Māra</s>. (42)
For even from great fury, set upon to destroy [you],
patience finds no excessive burden — especially when it is firmly established in its proper vessel. (43)
But that immediately following the victory over <s>Māra</s>, the very great destruction of the afflictions

children.text: tasyām eva kṛtaṃ rātrau tad eva paramādbhutam || 44
children.translated_text: was accomplished in that very night — that indeed is supremely wondrous. (44)
The sun with its thousand rays, which dispels darkness —

children.text: vīra vismayam āgacchet sa tīrthyavijaye tava || 45
children.translated_text: even it, O hero, would be struck with wonder at your conquest of the <s>tīrthikas</s> (heretics). (45)
The passionate by the passionless, the wrathful by one who has conquered wrath,

children.text: mūḍho vigatamohena tribhir nityaṃ jitās trayaḥ || 46
children.translated_text: the deluded by one free from delusion — always the three are conquered by the three. (46)
You praise true <s>dharmas</s> and censure false <s>dharmas</s>;

children.text: anurodhavirodhau ca na staḥ sadasatos tava || 47
children.translated_text: yet neither approval nor disapproval for the virtuous or the non-virtuous exists in you. (47)
Neither toward <s>Arhats</s> nor toward <s>tīrthikas</s>, with respect to hostility or affection,

children.text: yasya te cetaso 'nyatvaṃ tasya te kā stutir bhavet || 48
children.translated_text: is there any change in your mind — for such a one as you, what praise could suffice? (48)

children.text: guṇeṣv api na saṅgo 'bhūt tṛṣṇā na guṇavatsv api |
children.translated_text: Even in virtues there was no attachment, no craving even toward those possessing virtues —
ah, the complete purity of your serene being! (49)
By the perpetual, unfailing serenity of your faculties,

children.text: mano nityaprasannaṃ te pratyakṣam iva dṛśyate || 50
children.translated_text: your ever-serene mind is seen as if directly perceptible. (50)
Even to children, the purities of your intellect and mindfulness are well known,
conveyed by your well-spoken words and graceful conduct, which reveal your inner nature. (51)

children.text: upaśāntaṃ ca kāntaṃ ca dīptam apratighāti ca |
children.translated_text: Peaceful and lovely, radiant and unopposed,

children.text: nibhṛtaṃ corjitaṃ cedaṃ rūpaṃ kam iva nākṣipet || 52
children.translated_text: serene yet majestic — this form of yours, whom would it not captivate? (52)

children.text: yenāpi śataśo dṛṣṭaṃ yo 'pi tatpūrvam īkṣate |
children.translated_text: Whether one has seen it hundreds of times, or whether one beholds it for the first time,

children.text: rūpaṃ prīṇāti te cakṣuḥ samaṃ tad ubhayor api || 53
children.translated_text: your form delights the eye equally for both. (53)

children.text: asecanakabhāvād dhi saumyabhāvāc ca te vapuḥ |
children.translated_text: For, due to its inexhaustible charm and its gentle nature, your body

children.text: darśane darśane prītiṃ vidadhāti navāṃ navām || 54
children.translated_text: at each and every viewing bestows ever-new delight. (54)
Your body is endowed with the qualities of its foundation; your qualities with the qualities of their master —
both endowed with supreme excellence, mutually befitting each other. (55)

children.text: kvānyatra suniviṣṭāḥ syur ime tāthāgatā guṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: Where else could these qualities of a <s>Tathāgata</s> be so well established,
other than in this very form of yours, resplendent with the major and minor marks? (56)

children.text: dhanyam asmīti te rūpaṃ vadatīvāśritān guṇān |
children.translated_text: Your form seems to say 'I am fortunate' regarding the virtues it hosts,

children.text: sunikṣiptā vayam iti pratyāhur iva tad guṇāḥ || 57
children.translated_text: and those virtues seem to reply 'we are well placed.' (57)

children.text: sarvam evāviśeṣeṇa kleśair baddham idaṃ jagat |
children.translated_text: This entire world without exception is bound by afflictions;
you, for the sake of liberating the world from afflictions, were long bound by compassion. (58)

children.text: kaṃ nu prathamato vande tvāṃ mahākaruṇām uta |
children.translated_text: Whom shall I first salute — you, or great compassion?

children.text: yayaivam api doṣajñas tvaṃ saṃsāre dhṛtaś ciram || 59
children.translated_text: By which, though knowing its faults, you were held in <s>saṃsāra</s> for so long. (59)
That you, accustomed to the happiness of solitude, yet amidst crowds, spent

children.text: kālā labdhaprasarayā tat te karuṇayā kṛtam || 60
children.translated_text: your time — that was done by your compassion, which had found its scope. (60)

children.text: śāntād araṇyād grāmāntaṃ tvaṃ hi nāga iva hradāt |
children.translated_text: From the peaceful forest to the village, like an elephant from a lake,
you are drawn by compassion, for the sake of those to be trained, as if by a spell. (61)
Though established in supreme tranquility, through the impelling power of compassion,
You were made to perform dance steps even in the arts of actors and performers. || 62

children.text: ṛddhir yā siṃhanādā ye svaguṇodbhāvanāś ca yāḥ |
children.translated_text: Whatever supernatural powers, whatever lion's roars, and whatever proclamations of your own virtues there were —
for you who had abandoned desire and self-regard, that was the touchstone of your compassion. || 63
Exclusively benevolent toward others' welfare, yet harsh upon her own abode —
only toward you alone, O Lord, was compassion uncompassionate. || 64

children.text: tathā hi kṛtvā śatadhā dhīrā balim iva kva cit |
children.translated_text: For indeed, the bold one, having broken you into a hundred pieces like an offering,
scattered you in all directions for the accomplishment of others' purposes. || 65
Yet clearly she acts in accordance with your own wish;

children.text: tathā hi bādhamānāpi tvāṃ satī nāparādhyate || 66
children.translated_text: for even though she afflicts you, being faithful, she does not offend. || 66
Well-worded, profound in meaning, truthful, and sweet;
having both hidden and manifest meanings, both concise and elaborate — || 67

children.text: kasya na syād upaśrutya vākyāny evaṃvidhāni te |
children.translated_text: who, upon hearing such words of yours, would not have
the conviction 'He is omniscient,' even one who had opposed you? || 68

children.text: prāyeṇa madhuraṃ sarvam agatyā kiṃ cid anyathā |
children.translated_text: For the most part all is sweet, occasionally otherwise out of necessity;

children.text: vākyaṃ tavārthasiddhyā tu sarvam eva subhāṣitam || 69
children.translated_text: but by the accomplishment of its purpose, all your speech is truly well-spoken. || 69

children.text: yac chlakṣṇaṃ yac ca paruṣaṃ yad vā tadubhayānvitam |
children.translated_text: Whether smooth, whether harsh, or endowed with both —

children.text: sarvam evaikarasatāṃ vimarde yāti te vacaḥ || 70
children.translated_text: all your speech, when examined closely, attains a single flavor. || 70
Ah, the supreme skill of thoroughly purified deeds,

children.text: yair idaṃ vākyaratnānām īdṛśaṃ bhājanaṃ kṛtam || 71
children.translated_text: by which this vessel for such jewels of speech was created! || 71
From this face, beautiful to the eyes,

children.text: mukhāt kṣarati te vākyaṃ candrād dravam ivāmṛtam || 72
children.translated_text: flows forth your speech, captivating to the ears, like liquid nectar from the moon. || 72
Your speech becomes like a rain cloud in allaying the dust of passion;
it becomes like <s>Garuḍa</s> in extracting the serpent of hatred. || 73
It becomes like the sun in further dispelling the darkness of ignorance;
it becomes like <s>Indra</s>'s thunderbolt in splitting the mountains of pride. || 74
Unfailing because it deals with what is directly seen, unconfused because it is free from defilements,

children.text: gamakaṃ suprayuktatvāt trikalyāṇaṃ hi te vacaḥ || 75
children.translated_text: communicative because it is well-applied — your speech is indeed beautiful in three ways. || 75

children.text: manāṃsi tāvac chrotṝṇāṃ haranty ādau vacāṃsi te |
children.translated_text: Your words first captivate the minds of listeners,

children.text: tato vimṛśyamānāni rajāṃsi ca tamāṃsi ca || 76
children.translated_text: and then, when reflected upon, they remove both passion and darkness. || 76
A comfort to the afflicted, an alarm to the heedless,

children.text: saṃvejanaṃ ca sukhināṃ yogavāhi vacas tava || 77
children.translated_text: and a stirring to the comfortable — your speech is potent like a healing remedy. || 77
Generating delight in the wise, increasing the intellect of the middling,

children.text: timiraghnaṃ ca mandānāṃ sārvajanyam idaṃ vacaḥ || 78
children.translated_text: and destroying the darkness of the dull — this speech is beneficial to all. || 78
It draws one away from wrong views, draws one near to <s>nirvāṇa</s>,
extracts faults, and rains down virtues — such is your speech. || 79
Your intellect is unobstructed everywhere, your mindfulness is present everywhere;

children.text: avandhyaṃ tena sarvatra sarvaṃ vyākaraṇaṃ tava || 80
children.translated_text: therefore all your pronouncements are unfailing everywhere. || 80

children.text: yan nādeśe na cākāle naivāpātre pravartase |
children.translated_text: Since you do not speak in the wrong place, nor at the wrong time, nor to an unworthy recipient,

children.text: vīryaṃ samyag ivārabdhaṃ tenāmoghaṃ vacas tava || 81
children.translated_text: like effort rightly undertaken, your speech is therefore never in vain. || 81
The one path, with easy means, self-consistent, free from danger,
beautiful in the beginning, middle, and end — such is your teaching, and no one else's. || 82
If the foolish, through attachment to their views, thus condemn

children.text: mataṃ yadi vigarhanti nāsti dṛṣṭisamo ripuḥ || 83
children.translated_text: your doctrine that is absolutely beautiful, there is no enemy equal to wrong views. || 83

children.text: anvabhuṅkthā yad asyārthe jagato vyasanaṃ bahu |
children.translated_text: Remembering the many sufferings you endured

children.text: tat saṃsmṛtya virūpe 'pi stheyaṃ te śāsane bhavet || 84
children.translated_text: for the sake of this world, one should remain steadfast in your teaching, even when it seems unappealing. || 84

children.text: prāg eva hitakartuś ca hitavaktuś ca śāsanam |
children.translated_text: How much more should the teaching of one who both does good and speaks good

children.text: kathaṃ na nāma kāryaṃ syād ādīptaśirasāpi te || 85
children.translated_text: be followed, even with one's head on fire? || 85
Liberation, the bliss of <s>bodhi</s> (awakening), reverence for your virtues, and tranquility —
all this fourfold good is obtained from your teaching. || 86
A terror to all heretics, a torment to <s>Namuchi</s> (Māra),
a comfort to gods and men — this is your teaching, O hero. || 87
Vast as the three realms, unattached, and irresistible —
even the dominion of Death has been conquered by your teaching. || 88
For one who knows the way of your teaching could remain even for an eon if he wished;

children.text: prayāti tatra tu svairī yatra mṛtyor agocaraḥ || 89
children.translated_text: but being free, he goes to where death has no dominion. || 89
The threefold division of time — for scriptural study, for contemplation of meaning,
and for meditative cultivation — exists in no teaching other than yours. || 90
That they do not revere this teaching of yours, O bull among sages,

children.text: śāsanaṃ nādriyante yat kiṃ vaiśasataraṃ tataḥ || 91
children.translated_text: so filled with goodness — what could be more tragic than that? || 91
Hearing about you satisfies, seeing you inspires faith,
your speech delights, and your teaching liberates. || 92

children.text: prasūtir harṣayati te vṛddhir nandayati prajāḥ |
children.translated_text: Your birth brings joy, your growth gladdens people,
your activity bestows grace, and your cessation brings sorrow. || 93
Praising you removes sin, remembering you brings delight,
seeking you produces wisdom, and fully knowing you purifies. || 94
Approaching you brings fortune, attending you supremely bestows understanding,
devotion to you removes fear, and worshiping you brings happiness. || 95
Pure through the perfection of moral conduct, clear through the perfection of meditation,
unperturbed through the perfection of wisdom — you are a great lake filled with merit. || 96
Your form is a jewel for seeing, your well-spoken words a jewel for hearing,
your <s>Dharma</s> a jewel for contemplation — you are indeed a mine of precious virtues. || 97

children.text: tvam oghair uhyamānānāṃ dvīpas trāṇaṃ kṣatātmanām |
children.translated_text: You are an island for those swept by floods, a protector for the wounded,
a refuge for those who fear existence, and the highest goal for those seeking liberation. || 98
A worthy vessel due to your pure conduct, a good field due to the abundance of fruit,
and a true friend due to your beneficence — to all living beings. || 99
You are dear because of your helpfulness, enchanting because of your delightfulness,
absolutely beautiful because of your gentleness, esteemed by all for your virtues. || 100
You are heartwarming because of your faultlessness, charming because of the excellence of your speech and form,
blessed because of the accomplishment of all purposes, and auspicious because of your abode in virtue. || 101
You are the encircler of those who stand firm, the restrainer of those who go astray,
the straightener of the crooked, and the impeller of the slow-moving. || 102
You harness the tamed to the yoke and disregard the incorrigible;
thus you are the supreme excellent charioteer of those who can be tamed among men. || 103
Your compassion is for those in distress, your desire for welfare is for those who are well,
your pity is for those in calamity, and your wish for benefit is for all. || 104

children.text: viruddheṣv api vātsalyaṃ pravṛttiḥ patiteṣv api |
children.translated_text: Affection even for those who oppose you, engagement even with the fallen,

children.text: raudreṣv api kṛpālutvaṃ kā nāmeyaṃ tavāryatā || 105
children.translated_text: mercy even toward the cruel — what indeed is this nobility of yours? || 105
If the authority of mother and father is acknowledged because of their beneficence,
how great then must be the authority vested in you, the supremely beneficent one! || 106
For those who are heedless of their own welfare, hostile as if to themselves,
standing at the edge of a precipice — you have become a rampart. || 107
For the benefit of both worlds and for the transcending of the world,
you have created the light of wisdom in worlds engulfed in darkness. || 108
The ways of life of gods and humans, though different in their enjoyments,
have come to unity in you through the common sharing of the <s>Dharma</s>. || 109
Transcending birth, age, caste, place, and time —

children.text: tvayā hi bhagavan dharmasarvātithyam idam kṛtam || 110
children.translated_text: this universal hospitality of the <s>Dharma</s> has been established by you, O <s>Bhagavān</s>. || 110
The gods, with folded hands, attend with wonder upon your <s>śrāvakas</s> who are beyond wonder,

children.text: upāsate prāñjalayaḥ śrāvakān api te surāḥ || 111
children.translated_text: desiring those who are beyond desire. || 111
Ah, the splendor of the arising of a Buddha in the circle of <s>saṃsāra</s> —
where human birth has become desirable even to the gods! || 112
Weariness, loss of the happiness of tranquility, contact with the unvirtuous,

children.text: dvaṃdvāny ākīrṇatā ceti doṣān guṇavad udvahan || 113
children.translated_text: dualities, and crowding — bearing these faults as if they were virtues, || 113
you strive for the welfare of the world with an unattached mind.
What indeed is that blessed <s>buddhadharmatā</s> (Buddha-nature) of the Buddhas? || 114

children.text: kadannāny api bhuktāni kva cit kṣud adhivāsitā |
children.translated_text: Even poor food was eaten, sometimes hunger was endured,

children.text: panthāno viṣamāḥ kṣuṇṇāḥ suptaṃ gokaṇṭakeṣv api || 115
children.translated_text: rough roads were trodden, and sleep was taken even on thorns. || 115
Reproaches were received, services concealed, disguises and strange languages adopted —
O Lord, out of affection for those to be trained, by you who are indeed the master. || 116

children.text: prabhutvam api te nātha sadā nātmani vidyate |
children.translated_text: Your mastery, O Lord, never rests upon yourself;

children.text: vaktavya iva sarvair hi svairaṃ svārthe niyujyase || 117
children.translated_text: for you are freely employed by all in their own interest, as if you were one who should be commanded. || 117

children.text: yena kena cid eva tvaṃ yatra tatra yathā tathā |
children.translated_text: By whomever, wherever, however
you are urged, you do not transgress your own excellent course of conduct. || 118
People are not as devoted to benefiting even those who benefit them,
as you are devoted to benefiting even those who seek to harm you. || 119
Toward an enemy who brings harm, you are a friend who brings benefit;
even toward one perpetually seeking faults, you are intent on finding virtues. || 120
Where there was an invitation to you with poison and with fire,

children.text: tatrābhūd abhisaṃyānaṃ sadayaṃ sāmṛtaṃ ca te || 121
children.translated_text: there your approach was full of compassion and accompanied by the nectar of immortality. || 121

children.text: ākroṣṭāro jitāḥ kṣāntyā drugdhāḥ svastyayanena ca |
children.translated_text: Revilers were conquered by your patience, those who harmed you by your blessing,
slanderers by your truthfulness, and those who would kill you by your loving-kindness. || 122
The many dispositions of men, ingrained from beginningless time —
you, having revealed their dangers, transformed them in an instant. || 123

children.text: yat sauratyaṃ gatās tīkṣṇāḥ kadaryāś ca vadānyatām |
children.translated_text: That the fierce have attained gentleness, the miserly generosity,
and the cruel have come to tenderness — that is your <s>upāyakauśala</s> (skill in means). || 124
The calming of the senses in <s>Nanda</s>, and humility in the pride-stiffened,

children.text: kṣamitvaṃ cāṅgulīmāle kaṃ na vismayam ānayet || 125
children.translated_text: and the forbearance of <s>Aṅgulimāla</s> — whom would these not bring to amazement? || 125
Many steadfast ones, having abandoned golden couches,

children.text: aśerata sukhaṃ dhīrās tṛptā dharmarasasya te || 126
children.translated_text: slept happily on beds of grass, satisfied with the taste of your <s>Dharma</s>. || 126

children.text: pṛṣṭenāpi kva cin noktam upetyāpi kathā kṛtā |
children.translated_text: Even when asked, in some cases you did not speak; even approaching, you engaged in conversation;
having aroused longing, you spoke elsewhere — by you who knew the right time and disposition. || 127
First producing receptivity in the mind through talks on generosity and so forth,

children.text: tato dharmo gatamale vastre raṅga ivārpitaḥ || 128
children.translated_text: then the <s>Dharma</s> was applied like dye upon a cloth from which the stain has been removed. || 128

children.text: na so 'sty upāyaḥ śaktir vā yena na vyāyataṃ tava |
children.translated_text: There is no means or power by which you have not exerted yourself
to lift the wretched world from the dreadful abyss of <s>saṃsāra</s>. || 129
Many and multiform were the words and deeds
that you performed here and there according to the different dispositions of those to be trained. || 130
All were pure, non-contradictory, worthy of worship and veneration,

children.text: sarvāṇy eva nṛdevānāṃ hitāni mahitāni ca || 131
children.translated_text: beneficial and honored by both gods and men. || 131

children.text: na hi vaktuṃ ca kartuṃ ca bahu sādhu ca śakyate |
children.translated_text: It is not possible to both speak and act in abundance and excellently;
yet both were seen in you, whose words never contradicted deeds. || 132
By your self-purification alone the world would be purified,

children.text: yasmān naivaṃvidhaṃ kṣetraṃ triṣu lokeṣe vidyate || 133
children.translated_text: since no such field of merit is found in the three worlds. || 133
How much more so, since you have thus exerted yourself in the beginningless strait of existence

children.text: hitāya sarvasattvānāṃ yas tvam evaṃ samudyataḥ || 134
children.translated_text: for the benefit of all beings who are utterly lost! || 134

children.text: na tāṃ pratipadaṃ vedmi syād yayāpacitis tava |
children.translated_text: I do not know that course of conduct by which one could repay you;

children.text: api ye parinirvānti te 'pi te nānṛṇā janāḥ || 135
children.translated_text: even those who attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — even they are not free from debt to you. || 135

children.text: tava te 'vasthitā dharme svārtham eva tu kurvate |
children.translated_text: Those who abide in your <s>Dharma</s> accomplish only their own welfare;

children.text: yaḥ śramas tannimittaṃ tu tava kā tasya niṣkṛtiḥ || 136
children.translated_text: but the labor you endured on their account — what is the recompense for that? || 136

children.text: tvaṃ hi jāgarṣi suptānāṃ saṃtānāny avalokayan |
children.translated_text: For you remain awake, watching over the mind-streams of those who sleep —
vigilant, a kinsman of good fortune to heedless beings. || 137
The destruction of the <s>kleśas</s> (defilements) has been proclaimed, the illusions of <s>Māra</s> have been shattered,
the wretchedness of <s>saṃsāra</s> has been declared, and the direction of fearlessness has been shown. || 138
What else should be done by one desiring the welfare of beings, out of compassion,

children.text: karaṇīyaṃ bhaved yatra na dattānunayo bhavān || 139
children.translated_text: where you have not already given your loving attention? || 139

children.text: yadi saṃcāriṇo dharmāḥ syur ime niyataṃ tvayā |
children.translated_text: If these virtues were transferable, they would surely have been bestowed by you
everywhere, beginning with <s>Devadatta</s>. || 140
Therefore, O Lord of the world, you have spoken the truth:

children.text: iti tvam uktavān bhūtaṃ jagat saṃjñapayann iva || 141
children.translated_text: 'Here, no one is the agent of another' — as if awakening the world. || 141
Having long set the true <s>Dharma</s> in motion on earth out of compassion for the world,
having produced many true disciples capable of benefiting the three worlds, || 142
and having directly trained those in your circle of disciples ending with <s>Subhadra</s> —

children.text: ṛṇaśeṣaṃ kim adyāpi sattveṣu yad abhūt tava || 143
children.translated_text: was there still a remaining debt to beings that was yours? || 143
You who pulverized your bones to sesame-like particles with the thunderbolt of <s>samādhi</s> —
even at the end you did not relinquish your commitment to the supremely difficult. || 144

children.text: parārthāv eva me dharmarūpakāyāv iti tvayā |
children.translated_text: 'Both my <s>dharmakāya</s> and <s>rūpakāya</s> are solely for the benefit of others' —
this you demonstrated to this reluctant world even in <s>nirvāṇa</s>. || 145

children.text: tathā hi satsu saṃkrāmya dharmakāyam aśeṣataḥ |
children.translated_text: For indeed, having transmitted the <s>dharmakāya</s> entirely to the virtuous,
and having divided the <s>rūpakāya</s> into fragments, you attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. || 146

children.text: aho sthitir aho vṛttam aho rūpam aho guṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: Ah, the steadfastness! Ah, the conduct! Ah, the form! Ah, the virtues!

children.text: na nāma buddhadharmāṇām asti kiṃ cid anadbhutam || 147
children.translated_text: There is nothing among the qualities of a Buddha that is not wonderful. || 147
Even against you who are beneficent, beautiful to behold, and of peaceful speech and bodily action,

children.text: tvayy api pratihanyante paśya mohasya raudratām || 148
children.translated_text: they strike — behold the ferocity of delusion! || 148
You who are an ocean of merit, a treasure of jewels, a mass of <s>Dharma</s>, a mine of virtues —

children.text: ye tvāṃ sattvā namasyanti tebhyo 'pi sukṛtaṃ namaḥ || 149
children.translated_text: those beings who pay homage to you, homage to their good fortune as well! || 149

children.text: akṣayās te guṇā nātha śaktis tu kṣayiṇī mama |
children.translated_text: Your virtues are inexhaustible, O Lord, but my power is limited;
therefore I stop, not from satisfaction, but from fear of endless elaboration. || 150
Immeasurable, innumerable, inconceivable, beyond comparison —

children.text: svayam evātmanātmānaṃ tvam eva jñātum arhasi || 151
children.translated_text: only you yourself are able to know yourself. || 151
Not even a fraction of your virtues has been praised,

children.text: parā ca nas tuṣṭir avasthitā hṛdi |
children.translated_text: yet supreme satisfaction abides in our hearts;
for indeed, the thirsts of people are quenched
merely without drawing from the waters of a great lake. || 152
By the ripening of this meritorious deed,
born of the inspiration of the <s>Muni</s>'s grace,
may the minds of beings, driven by the wind of disturbing wrong thoughts,
come under control. || 153
